chapter: Leading his own band in Los Angeles
title: Armstrong's California records and Leon Herriford
summary: Dance and Clayton discuss Armstrong's California recordings, the Leon Herriford band, and Armstrong's liking for Guy Lombardo.

story.theme_name: Working with and around Louis Armstrong
story.community_name: Playing with and around Louis Armstrong

blocks.x: You know those records they made there with Lionel Hampton and Lawrence Brown... from Dumas
Yes, 'Ding Dong Daddy 'Confessing'.
Yes. when, when, I mean I know he'd the important ones had been (?) once before, but I think an these gave him extra.....
Yes, I do too. I do too. than 'Cornet Choo Sney' and those things. A different style Played some pretty things, beautiful things. And I liked the fast ones. I liked everything he did.
And he played here in another band named Leon Herriford.
Herriford?
Herriford, yes. Yes, he sounded like Guy Lombardo. The saxophone & vibrato. Those Louis made with him ?). You ever heard records
No, what, no, Leon Herriford?
Yes, Leon Herriford. Yes.
Well, which record is that?

That was before Hite. Now I don't remember now which ones he made, but All those California records weren't just made by just Les Hite. Because Leon Herriford was in the Cotton Club before Hite went in.
Herriford is HERRIFORD?
HERRIFORD. HERRIFORD, I believe, Herriford.
Oh, HERRIford.
Yes.
Well I was under the impression that, let me see, I was thinking of, I think you'll have to check this, but I was thinking that the 'Ding Dong Daddy' records.....
Well that might have been made.......
I think that Russell's band..
Well you see he made some inbetween California now.
Yes he did. Well I can easily check that. I mean, you'd know. Then of course Louis always did say that he liked Guy Lombardo's band.
Yes. Yes he did. He always said it and I think he meant it. He played with him didn't he out in Long Island?
Yes. But I think it's, I think you can see what it was he liked. You know, the sort of, well 'Sweethearts on Parade' was another one of his big things. That was a Guy Lombardo thing wasn't it?
Yes, right.
